content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"This judge text compares the challenger's seed/loins chain against the defender's chain and uses whether it names Joseph as the begetter as a defect, so it applies the verse-by-verse stating test the rule governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"Phrase: 'chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse.' Readings weighed: (1) 'does not name Joseph as the begetter' is a forbidden verse-by-verse stating test; (2) it is merely a chain-footing gap. I read it as (1).","why":"The judge treats the absence of a verse naming Joseph as the begetter as a defect, which is the retired stating-verse test rather than chain-against-chain footing."}
